name: Carlos Castaneda
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Castaneda was studying art in Peru before emigrating to the US at 25 in 1951. His first book, The Teachings of Don Juan, was published in 1968 at age 42-43.

name: Roger Moore
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Moore had bit parts and an MGM contract by 1953 (age 25-26), but his breakout role as The Saint came in 1962 at age 35, and James Bond fame came in 1973 at age 46.

name: Yukio Mishima
milestone_by_age_26: Published first short story 'Hanazakari no mori' at 16 in Bungei Bunka magazine (1941), first collection at 19 (1944), and breakthrough novel Confessions of a Mask at 24 (1949), establishing him as a major Japanese literary voice.
early_history_summary: Mishima began writing stories at age 12 while attending the elite Gakushūin (Peers School) in Tokyo. At 16, his short story was published in the literary magazine Bungei Bunka under a pen name given by his teacher to protect him from his father's disapproval. His first collection followed at 19, and his semi-autobiographical novel Confessions of a Mask at 24 cemented his literary reputation.
family_context_summary: Father was a government official in the Ministry of Agriculture and Commerce; grandmother Natsuko was descended from samurai aristocracy (granddaughter of a daimyō related to Tokugawa Ieyasu) and raised Mishima in her household until age 12, exposing him to classical Japanese arts.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a government official; mother's father was a scholar of Chinese classics and principal of Kaisei Academy. Grandmother Natsuko had aristocratic samurai lineage and cultivated Mishima's appreciation for classical Japanese culture including Kabuki and Noh.
primary_early_advantage_tags: elite school, samurai lineage, literary mentor, aristocratic grandmother
evidence_summary: Mishima attended the elite Gakushūin (Peers School) and began writing at age 12, publishing his first story at 16 in Bungei Bunka magazine. His grandmother, descended from samurai aristocracy, raised him in a culturally rich but oppressive household. His teacher Fumio Shimizu mentored him and facilitated his literary debut. By 24, his novel Confessions of a Mask established him as a major Japanese literary figure.

name: Françoise Hardy
milestone_by_age_26: Released debut single 'Tous les garçons et les filles' in 1962 at age 18, which sold over a million copies and made her a European star overnight; debut album released same year, and she represented Monaco at Eurovision in 1963.
early_history_summary: Hardy grew up in Paris raised by a single mother who worked as an accountant's assistant. She received a guitar from her absent father as a teenager and began writing songs while studying at the Sorbonne. After failing an initial audition, she signed with Disques Vogue in late 1961 and released her breakthrough single in 1962, becoming an instant yé-yé star.
family_context_summary: Raised by a single mother who worked as an accountant's assistant in Paris; her absent father bought her a guitar after being convinced by her mother. The family lived modestly.
primary_early_advantage_tags: yé-yé wave, Paris music scene, radio distribution, natural star quality
evidence_summary: Hardy grew up in modest circumstances in Paris with a single mother. She received a guitar as a teenager and began writing songs while at the Sorbonne. After signing with Disques Vogue at 17, her 1962 debut single 'Tous les garçons et les filles' sold over a million copies, propelled by radio play on Salut les copains. She became an instant star of the yé-yé movement at 18.

name: Arno Allan Penzias
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Penzias graduated with a BS in physics from CCNY in 1954 and served in the Army Signal Corps before enrolling at Columbia in 1956. His PhD was completed in 1962 (age 29) and the cosmic microwave background discovery came in 1964 (age 31).

name: N. R. Narayana Murthy
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Murthy earned his bachelor's (1967) and master's from IIT Kanpur (1969) and worked as a systems programmer at IIM Ahmedabad, but founded Infosys in 1981 at age 35.

name: Kanye West
milestone_by_age_26: Produced multiple tracks on Jay-Z's landmark album The Blueprint (2001) at age 24, becoming one of hip-hop's most sought-after producers; signed solo deal with Roc-A-Fella Records in 2002 and released debut album The College Dropout in February 2004 at age 26.
early_history_summary: West began making beats at age 14 in Chicago, saving his allowance to buy a sampler. He sold his first beat for Jermaine Dupri's 1998 album at 21. He became an in-house producer for Roc-A-Fella Records, with his chipmunk soul production style gaining major recognition through his work on Jay-Z's The Blueprint in 2001. Despite industry resistance to him as a rapper, he signed a solo deal and released The College Dropout in 2004.
family_context_summary: Mother Donda West was a professor and chair of the English Department at Chicago State University; father Ray West was a former Black Panther and one of the first black photojournalists at The Atlanta Journal-Constitution. Parents divorced when Kanye was 3; raised by mother in Chicago's middle-class South Shore neighborhood.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was an English professor at Chicago State University, providing an academic and culturally rich environment. Father was a photojournalist and political activist. Neither parent had direct music industry connections.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Chicago hip-hop scene, Roc-A-Fella network, chipmunk soul production, early beat-making, mentor No I.D.
evidence_summary: West grew up in Chicago's middle-class South Shore with his mother, a university professor. He began producing beats at 14 and sold his first beat at 21. His distinctive chipmunk soul production style on Jay-Z's The Blueprint (2001) at age 24 made him one of hip-hop's most sought-after producers. He was embedded in the Roc-A-Fella Records ecosystem and mentored by producer No I.D. in Chicago. Despite industry resistance to him as a rapper, he released The College Dropout at 26.

name: George Miller
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Miller was studying medicine at the University of New South Wales in his early 20s. His first feature film, Mad Max, was released in 1979 at age 34.

name: Woody Allen
milestone_by_age_26: Began writing jokes for TV comedians at 16 (1952), joined NBC staff, wrote for Sid Caesar and other major shows, won Sylvania Award for television writing at 21 (1957), and began performing as a stand-up comedian by 25 (1961).
early_history_summary: Allen (born Allan Stewart Konigsberg) began writing jokes while still in high school in Brooklyn, selling material to newspaper columnists and TV comedians at 16. He joined NBC's writing staff and wrote for Sid Caesar, The Ed Sullivan Show, and The Tonight Show. He won a Sylvania Award in 1957 for his work on The Sid Caesar Show at age 21, establishing himself as one of television's top comedy writers before transitioning to stand-up comedy.
family_context_summary: Born to Nettie (née Cherry), a bookkeeper at her family's delicatessen, and Martin Konigsberg, a jewelry engraver and waiter, in Brooklyn. Working-class Jewish family.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Parents were working-class; no direct entertainment industry connections.
primary_early_advantage_tags: New York TV comedy, early joke writing, Sid Caesar, golden age of television, NBC
evidence_summary: Allen grew up in a working-class Jewish family in Brooklyn and began writing jokes for TV comedians at 16. He joined NBC's writing staff and wrote for major shows including Sid Caesar's, winning a Sylvania Award at 21. New York City's golden age of television provided the ecosystem for his early career. By his mid-20s, he was one of television's top comedy writers and had begun performing as a stand-up comedian.

name: Peter J. Ratcliffe
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Ratcliffe was studying medicine at Cambridge and St Bartholomew's Hospital in his early-to-mid 20s. His doctorate was completed in 1987 (age 33) and Nobel Prize-winning work on oxygen sensing came in the 1990s.

name: Jean-Marie Balestre
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Balestre worked as a journalist after WWII, but his founding of the FFSA came in 1950 (age 29) and his FISA presidency in 1978 (age 57).

name: Robert Plant
milestone_by_age_26: Became lead singer of Led Zeppelin in 1968 at age 20; band released five landmark albums by 1973 including Led Zeppelin IV (1971) with 'Stairway to Heaven,' making Plant the frontman of one of the biggest rock bands in the world by his mid-20s.
early_history_summary: Plant left school at 16 to pursue singing in local blues bands in the English Midlands, including the Crawling King Snakes and Band of Joy with drummer John Bonham. He cut three obscure singles on CBS Records and worked various jobs including laying tarmac. In 1968, Jimmy Page discovered Plant singing with Hobbstweedle at a Birmingham teacher training college and recruited him for what became Led Zeppelin.
family_context_summary: Father Robert C. Plant was a qualified civil engineer who served in the RAF during WWII; mother Annie Celia Plant (née Cain) was described as Romani. Plant grew up in Halesowen, Worcestershire. His father disapproved of his music career and preferred he become an accountant.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a civil engineer who played violin as a young man; grandfather Robert Shropshire Plant founded and led the Vono Revo Works Band. Some musical heritage in the family but not professional music industry.
primary_early_advantage_tags: powerful voice, blues immersion, John Bonham collaboration, Midlands blues scene, early band experience
evidence_summary: Plant grew up in Halesowen with a civil engineer father who disapproved of his music ambitions. He left school at 16 to sing in local blues bands, including the Band of Joy with drummer John Bonham. His remarkable vocal ability — described as a 'primeval wail' — caught Jimmy Page's attention in 1968, leading to the formation of Led Zeppelin. By his mid-20s, Plant was the frontman of one of rock's biggest bands, with five landmark albums released by age 25.
